capabilities.test: Top-level README/index organizes content by difficulty or progression (Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced or Phase N/Unit N)
At least one lesson ships runnable code in more than one programming language (e.g. Python + TypeScript/Rust/Julia)
Repo includes lessons/projects covering LLM usage, RAG, and agents (the modern stack)
Repo has dedicated MCP lessons/projects showing how to build or use MCP servers/clients
Repo teaches at least one core algorithm (attention, transformer, optimizer) implemented from scratch alongside the production library version
Lessons can be run without local setup (browser IDE, Colab notebook, or Pyodide/WebAssembly)
Repo provides a way for learners to find their starting level (placement quiz, skill self-assessment, or roadmap prerequisite map)
Each lesson produces a concrete artifact the learner can take away (prompt, skill, agent, MCP server, notebook)
Curriculum has a public web-rendered view (static site, JupyterBook, GitHub Pages, or MkDocs)
Each lesson has a quiz or exercise that checks understanding (with answers provided)
Learner can see progress across lessons/units (persisted state, completion checkmarks, or syllabus-level percentage)
Repo has automated tests that validate runnable code blocks or notebooks on every PR
Repo ships an installable Python package (pip-installable) that mirrors the lesson content
Repo includes a setup guide covering Python/pip/uv/Docker paths so learners can run locally
